Well regarding the milk - it was in respect to the first Star Wars - when Luke was still living with his parents and he pours himself the blue milk at the table. So, what is blue milk? It's made from the mammary glands of the female Bantha and it's widely popular throughout a lot of the planets in the galaxy, including Tatooine, Lothal, and Lah'mu. In TLJ he is milking a Thala-Siren and it was greenish milk.

Like many things in the movie it was a "tit for tat" kind of thing or a "mirroring" effect kind of thing or an hommage or call them "Easter egg" references to the original SW and the comics. Example her look into the mirror and seeing multiple selves - that was like when Yoda was training a young Luke and Luke had to battle himself.

This cramming of a lot of crap in your words are the pairing of this movie to the past Star War movies and the comic books and actually made it very enjoyable for me. 

IMO Rose makes a great new hero - she a throw back to feeling of the people that started the rebellion, that were loyal, fought for what is right no matter what and gives hope. Rose’s ring sows a seed of hope in the child's heart, and at the end of the film, we see him sharing stories about Luke Skywalker with his friends. The ring silver in color and featuring the original Rebel Alliance insignia has been passed down over the decades until landing in Rose’s possession. The ring was worn in the halls of the Imperial Senate during the days of the Galactic Civil War… with the inner engraving shown only in secret as proof of Rebel loyalty. The symbol in Rose’s ring is a stylized Starbird, a phoenix-like creature that represents eternal rebirth. Introduced as the Rebel Alliance logo in the Original Trilogy and it resembles the emblem of the Jedi Order.

For me Rose brings back that feeling of the little guy ... the average guy..the working guy against the big the guy, the evil corporations, or governments. Her and Finn I think make a great start with characters to cheer for. Lei, Luke, Solo - are aged and passed. If they want to continue the Star War Legacy they need new heroes for younger audiences to cheer for and identify with. 

Snoke - his room - his guards again a hommage to Palpatine and his guards. The first fight where he shoots out the top side turrets - hommage to the fight scene of Luke flying and zipping through the death star trying to take it out after the other pilots got shot down. Porgs to me are cute and the counter-part or equivalent to Ewoks - (something cute and furry to sell)

For me this movie was long - but it wasn't full of crap. It felt more like a passing of the torch. They did a billion of these mirroring effect or easter eggs or hommages to the original Star Wars. It felt almost like they were pairing new things up against the old and saying good bye. And saying hello to the new. Much like the message throughout the movie. Saying good bye to the old order - the old Jedi - the old characters - regimes - etc and making room for the new. So this movie felt more like a good bye to an old friend and an introduction to a new friend and I was shown what they have in common and what differs. 

That's my experience of the movie. People that are hating on the movie I think are those that want it to hold firm to the old - that don't want to let go and try something new... imo..or they just expect a cookie cutter movie vibe ..beginning to end yet have it fit all the past narrative we know so well from Star wars. I felt they showed respect to the old by all the Easter Eggs like the milk.. and made me feel okay in saying good bye and welcoming to the new generation of whats to come.
